headers.//: Kept identical to Handler.csp() in vanilla/serve.py. A browser enforces the intersection of the header and the <meta> policy in index.html, so the two must not drift. No nonce and no hash are needed because the app has zero inline <script> tags.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.gstatic.com https://apis.google.com; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com; img-src 'self' data: blob: https://lh3.googleusercontent.com https://*.googleusercontent.com; connect-src 'self' https://*.googleapis.com https://*.firebaseio.com wss://*.firebaseio.com https://www.gstatic.com https://apis.google.com https://www.googleapis.com https://www.google-analytics.com https://*.google-analytics.com https://region1.google-analytics.com https://accounts.google.com https://*.firebaseapp.com https://*.googleusercontent.com; frame-src https://accounts.google.com https://*.firebaseapp.com https://*.web.app; worker-src 'self' blob:; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'self'; object-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'; upgrade-insecure-requests

headers.//: HTML must revalidate or a deploy never reaches anyone; hashed-ish assets are not content-hashed, so they get a short cache instead of immutable.
